PAPERS.title: Enhancing Urban Air Quality Mapping through Novel Measurement and Modelling approaches, and Citizen Science: Actionable Insights from the RI-URBANS Project
PAPERS.pm: Low-cost sensor networks, mobile platforms, citizen data
PAPERS.n: Cross-city synthesis of the RI-URBANS air-quality-mapping pilots: stationary low-cost sensor networks, mobile monitoring and citizen-collected data set against reference networks and modelling. Central operational finding is that harmonisation across methods, not sensor accuracy, is the binding constraint on comparability

PAPERS.title: Multi-Wavelength Optical Characterization of Carbonaceous Aerosols at a Coastal Urban Site in Genoa: Intercomparison of Real-Time and Filter-Based Techniques
PAPERS.pm: AE33 aethalometer vs MWAA and BLAnCA filter analysis
PAPERS.n: Urban coastal site, Multedo (Genoa). AE33 against two offline filter techniques across UV, visible and near-IR: R2 0.93-0.99, closest agreement MWAA vs BLAnCA. AE33 reads systematically 12-22% high depending on wavelength, implicating the default multiple-scattering correction. AAE near unity in all three

PAPERS.title: An accurate and sensitive method for identifying atmospheric alkylamines: selective enrichment by alkaline purging-acidic absorption coupled with ion chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry
PAPERS.pm: Speciated gas and PM-phase alkylamines by IC-MS/MS
PAPERS.n: Alkaline purging with acidic absorption enrichment ahead of IC-MS/MS. Method detection limits 9-94 pg m-3 gaseous and 0.1-1.1 pg m-3 in PM; resolves the dimethylamine / monoethylamine isobar and quantifies tertiary amines that derivatisation methods miss. Field-applied in Dalian septic tanks and traffic tunnels

PAPERS.title: In Situ Collection and Photochemical Aging of Individual Ship Plumes Captured at Sea
PAPERS.pm: Shipborne oxidation flow reactor on individual vessel plumes
PAPERS.n: Oxidation flow reactor operated from a mobile research vessel, probing named ocean-going ships at 0.6-1.6 km standoff in the Baltic. Gas and potential-aerosol mass emission factors measured fresh, then after photochemical aging: particle mass rose for every vessel, and secondary formation scaled with SO2 emission, i.e. fuel sulfur

PAPERS.title: Particulate matter removal by precipitation under normal and wildfire conditions across the United States using double machine learning
PAPERS.pm: Hourly EPA PM2.5 and PM10 vs NLDAS-2 precipitation
PAPERS.n: PREPRINT. 2014-2023 hourly records at 760 PM2.5 and 451 PM10 EPA monitors merged with NLDAS-2 meteorology and NOAA HMS smoke flags; DoubleML separates precipitation from confounding meteorology. Removal rises with rain intensity, particle size and initial load but falls as smoke loading rises. Washout coefficients a=0.0404/b=0.5951 (PM2.5), a=0.0812/b=0.4508 (PM10)

PAPERS.title: Seasonal predictability of winter PM2.5 pollution severity in India through a strong pollution-extratropical storm connection
PAPERS.pm: Government reference PM2.5 network, >10 winters
PAPERS.n: Quality-controlled Indian CPCB PM2.5 records. Western disturbances - Mediterranean-origin extratropical storms - explain about 70% of interannual winter PM2.5 variance across northern India via ventilation and wet removal. WD activity tracks to preceding-autumn North Atlantic and tropical Indian Ocean SST, giving one-season-ahead skill of r2 = 0.52-0.69

PAPERS.title: Multi-Point Prediction and Interpretable Analysis of Dust Concentration in Open-Pit Coal Mine During the Cold Season Using a Stacking Learning Framework
PAPERS.pm: Multi-point cold-season mine dust concentration
PAPERS.n: Metadata only - no abstract in Crossref per-DOI, Europe PMC or PubMed on the entry date. Title establishes a multi-point cold-season dust-concentration prediction task at an open-pit coal mine using a stacking ensemble with interpretability analysis. Sensor count, horizon, base learners and error figures are not recoverable and none is asserted

PAPERS.title: Spatiotemporal associations between PM2.5, greenspace, physical activity, and stress: a geographic ecological momentary assessment study in Hong Kong
PAPERS.pm: Mobile personal PM2.5, 5-600 min cumulative windows
PAPERS.n: 800 adults over two days: 1.7 million personal PM2.5 measurements, 2.1 million accelerometer records, 4,800 momentary assessments, eye-level greenspace from 4.3 million street-view images, analysed across eight activity-travel contexts with a DAG-guided double-ML framework. Higher PM2.5 tracked more light and less moderate-to-vigorous activity; context-specific estimates reversed sign

PAPERS.title: A calibrated, uncertainty-aware, and spatially explicit emission inventory of New Zealand's agricultural diesel tractor fleet
PAPERS.pm: Non-road machinery PM2.5, Monte Carlo uncertainty
PAPERS.n: 43,367 registered tractors, 31,253 active-licensed, 29,278 dealer sales 2017-2025; IPCC Tier 2 fuel-anchored, EMEP/EEA factors, tier hours calibrated against a CARB study, fuel anchored to a 204 Ml national target. 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo gives 115 t PM2.5 (95% UI 73-190) and 2258 t NOx. Gini 0.51 for PM2.5: top 30% of tractors emit 69%

PAPERS.title: Numerical study of a Saharan dust plume impact on radiation, urban climate and thermal comfort in the Paris region during an heatwave event
PAPERS.pm: CAMS dust aerosol in Meso-NH, AOD-validated
PAPERS.n: Three Meso-NH runs over Paris for the 15-19 June 2022 heatwave - no dust, CAMS dust, double CAMS dust - validated against the PANAME-Urban campaign for AOD and incoming solar radiation. Dust cuts surface shortwave by up to 75 W m-2 and air temperature by up to 1 C. Thermal-comfort gain of up to 1 C in sunlit areas only; in shade, added diffuse radiation, humidity and reduced wind cancel it

PAPERS.title: Real-world emissions of PM-bound environmentally persistent free radicals and reactive radical species generation from non-road construction equipment
PAPERS.pm: PM-bound environmentally persistent free radicals
PAPERS.n: Metadata only - no abstract retrievable on the entry date. Title establishes real-world (not dynamometer) measurement of PM-bound EPFRs and downstream reactive-radical generation from non-road construction equipment. Radical concentrations, engine tiers, duty cycles and the assay are not recoverable and none is asserted here

PAPERS.title: Associations of Fine Particulate Matter Components With Acute Aortic Dissection: A Time-Stratified Case-Crossover Study
PAPERS.pm: Component-resolved PM2.5: BC, OM, sulfate, nitrate
PAPERS.n: Hangzhou 2015-2023, conditional logistic regression plus weighted quantile sum. At lag 0-1 an IQR rise in black carbon, organic matter and sulfate gave 42% (OR 1.42, 1.15-1.75), 35% (1.35, 1.10-1.64) and 36% (1.36, 1.09-1.69) higher odds of Stanford type A dissection; type B positive but null. BC carried >50% of the joint WQS weight

PAPERS.title: Long-term ambient air pollution exposure, metabolomic signatures, and incident pulmonary hypertension: A large prospective cohort study
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5, PM10, NO2, NOx and a joint air pollution score
PAPERS.n: 444,346 participants with NMR metabolomics, 2,328 incident pulmonary hypertension over 13.58 y median. Air pollution score HR 1.12 per SD (1.08-1.17); individual pollutants 1.06-1.93 per 10 ug m-3. Elastic net gave a 105-metabolite signature (lipoproteins, fatty acids, amino acids) mediating 11.74% (7.91-18.95) of the score-PH association

PAPERS.title: Does Reported Sex Modifies the Association between Ambient Air Pollution exposure and Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementia? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
PAPERS.pm: Long-term PM2.5 and 11 further pollutants, F:M ratio
PAPERS.n: 24 cohorts, >126 million participants, searched to Sep 2025; female-to-male ratio of risk ratios as the modification metric, GRADE moderate. Null for Alzheimer's (PM2.5 RRR 0.963, 0.919-1.009) and vascular dementia (1.003, 0.954-1.054); the single positive is all-cause dementia (1.046, 1.024-1.069). Heterogeneity negligible except PM10 in AD (I2 61%)

PAPERS.title: Is passive smoking associated with acute stress response? An observational real-world study
PAPERS.pm: Self-reported secondhand smoke exposure, no measurement
PAPERS.n: 4,460 grassroots rescue personnel, self-administered ASD scale and PCL-5. Univariate OR 2.509 (1.621-3.883) for acute stress disorder and 3.298 (1.459-7.451) for PTSD; the PTSD association vanished on full adjustment (2.513, 0.900-5.151). Exposure is self-reported with no particle metric, the design cannot order exposure and outcome, and the reported multivariate ASD CI (1.959-3.144 around OR 1.990) is internally inconsistent

PAPERS.title: Evaluation of the effects of air pollutants on lung function using ambulatory monitor data from the MobiliSense Project
PAPERS.pm: Continuous personal BC and PM2.5 with GPS, 15 min-6 h lags
PAPERS.n: PREPRINT. 199 Paris adults 2018-2020 carrying two ambulatory pollutant monitors, GPS and an accelerometer; 2,504 spirometry tests, morning and evening over three days. Per 1 ug m-3 BC 1 h and 2 h before testing, FEV1 fell 0.016 L (-0.024, -0.008) and 0.021 L (-0.034, -0.007). PM2.5 at 15/30/60 min cut FEV1/FVC by 0.60, 0.70 and 0.50 pp

PAPERS.title: Breathing in harm: current insights into the effects of air pollution on cardiorespiratory health
PAPERS.pm: Ambient air pollution, no single exposure metric
PAPERS.n: Narrative review of mechanisms linking ambient pollution to cardiometabolic risk and cardiovascular death, with sections on heart failure, COPD and asthma exacerbation, on pregnancy, neonates, children and pre-existing disease, and on the COVID-19 lockdown natural experiment. No pooled estimate, no systematic search protocol, no PROSPERO registration - useful as an orientation map, not as evidence

PAPERS.title: Mid-to-Late Pregnancy: A Critical Window for the Protective Effect of Green Space Against Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
PAPERS.pm: Monthly residential PM2.5 alongside NDVI, -10 to +3 months
PAPERS.n: 1:3 age- and sex-matched case-control, 207 ASD children and 621 controls, central China. Monthly residential NDVI and PM2.5 from 10 months before to 3 months after birth in a DLNM. Cases had lower NDVI in all 14 months; the protective window is mid-to-late pregnancy. PM2.5 neither mediated nor modified the effect after Bonferroni correction - a clean null for the obvious confounding pathway

PAPERS.title: Association between air pollution and preeclampsia: a nationwide study from 2018 to 2023
PAPERS.pm: Ambient air pollution, nationwide registry linkage
PAPERS.n: Metadata only - the PubMed record carries no abstract and neither Crossref nor Europe PMC held one on the entry date. Title establishes a nationwide 2018-2023 study of ambient air pollution and preeclampsia. Country, pollutant set, case count, exposure model and effect direction are all unrecoverable; none is asserted here

PAPERS.title: Evaluating air cleaner effectiveness in schools: a comprehensive review and protocol of a cluster-randomized controlled trial of physicochemical and microbial markers
PAPERS.pm: Continuous PM10, PM4, PM2.5, PM1 plus CO2, T, RH, VOC
PAPERS.n: PROTOCOL, NCT07479420. 180 classrooms in 29 Dutch primary schools randomised to HEPA cleaners, ionisation/plasma cleaners or none, CADR-matched and lab-screened for safety; three-week baseline plus three three-week intervention periods, to 14 weeks per school. Electrostatic dustfall collectors for bacterial and viral markers, active sampling in 12 rooms for validation. No results yet

PAPERS.title: Smoke-Free Home Intervention in Permanent Supportive Housing: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial
PAPERS.pm: Secondhand smoke in multiunit housing, CO-verified
PAPERS.n: 40 San Francisco Bay Area permanent-supportive-housing sites, 400 residents (mean age 54.5), Jan 2022-Mar 2025. Primary outcome missed: 90-day smoke-free-home adoption 6.8% vs 4.8%, OR 1.45 (0.69-3.07). Any 1-day adoption 63.4% vs 36.8%, aOR 3.83 (2.63-5.57); 7-day CO-verified abstinence 6.3% vs 1.0%, OR 6.94 (1.69-28.45) on 14 events total

PAPERS.title: Inhalation risks of carbon fiber-reinforced plastic-derived emissions: Occupational exposure and regulatory perspectives
PAPERS.pm: Respirable CFRP fibre fragments and thermal ultrafines
PAPERS.n: Life-cycle review of CFRP emissions across manufacturing, machining, recycling and end-of-life. Mechanical processing yields respirable high-aspect-ratio fragments; thermal processing yields ultrafine particles plus hazardous gases. The review declines the asbestos and pathogenic-CNT analogy on the evidence available, but states plainly that chronic-exposure data are too thin to support any quantitative toxicity comparison

PAPERS.title: Study on the removal of condensable particulate matter from flue gas using string-of-beads liquid
PAPERS.pm: Condensable PM from coal and MSW incineration flue gas
PAPERS.n: Condensable PM is emitted as vapour and forms particles downstream of the stack, so it escapes filterable-PM controls entirely. String-of-beads liquid removed 29.56-65.27% overall at 1.17-8.25% of the energy of conventional condensation; organic fraction outperformed inorganic, SO4 fraction best at 78.34%. Condensation dominates hot, dissolution dominates as gas cools; a two-term model reproduces both. Bench scale only

PAPERS.title: Assessing intergenerational health equity in the mortality impacts of acute and chronic air pollution exposure
PAPERS.pm: Acute and chronic exposure, mortality impact attribution
PAPERS.n: Metadata only - no abstract retrievable on the entry date. Title establishes an intergenerational-equity framing applied to mortality impacts of both acute and chronic air pollution exposure, which is an unusual and potentially useful decomposition. The cohorts, discounting assumptions, pollutant set and geography are unrecoverable and none is asserted here

PAPERS.title: Trends and Determinants of Stroke Burden in Turkiye, 2000-2023: An Analysis Using Global Burden of Disease Data
PAPERS.pm: GBD ambient particulate matter risk-attributable fraction
PAPERS.n: GBD 2023 for Turkiye. Age-standardised stroke incidence 141.47 to 103.05, deaths 132.61 to 57.03, DALYs 2696.30 to 1073.51 per 100,000 over 2000-2023. In 2023 ambient particulate matter was the leading environmental risk at 11.93% of stroke deaths, against 21.29% for high blood pressure and 12.20% for smoking. Ecological, and GBD exposure surfaces are themselves modelled - not an independent measurement

PAPERS.title: Tire wear particles impact a roadside wild plant species
PAPERS.pm: Tire wear particles, non-exhaust traffic source
PAPERS.n: Controlled TWP exposure of Bromus catharticus, a common Japanese roadside weed. Both shoot and root growth were significantly inhibited and root malondialdehyde - a lipid peroxidation marker - rose significantly. Dose, particle size distribution and exposure route are the inference-limiting unknowns from the abstract, and a single annual grass cannot stand for roadside vegetation generally. Relevant here because TWP is the fastest-growing non-exhaust PM source and optical monitors size it poorly
